## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

<system-reminder>This memory is 6 days old. Memories are point-in-time observations, not live state — claims about code behavior or file:line citations may be outdated. Verify against current code before asserting as fact.</system-reminder>
1	---
2	name: project_lobu_ai_prod_db
3	description: Prod DB cluster is now lobu-ai-prod-db (replaced summaries-db) after the 2026-05-20 test-against-prod wipe + PITR recovery
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 023a3362-eb2f-4af1-958e-fb1aa8a9d18d
8	  modified: 2026-07-29T23:53:01.706Z
9	---
10	
11	On 2026-05-20 the `summaries-prod` production `owletto` database (49 orgs / 36 users / ~1.17M events, ~12GB) was **wiped**: a developer ran the integration test suite locally with `DATABASE_URL` pointed at prod; `__tests__/setup/test-db.ts` setup runs `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE` and the `summaries` role owns the DB, so it succeeded (ran ~16:59–17:27 UTC). NOT CI (CI uses throwaway `lobu_test`).
12	
13	**Recovery:** CNPG PITR from R2 backup lineage `summaries-db-v2` to 2026-05-20 16:00 UTC (latest verified-complete snapshot) into a NEW cluster **`lobu-ai-prod-db`** (clean name chosen by user). The old `summaries-db` was retired/deleted.
14	
15	**Current prod topology (CNPG on k8s, ns `summaries-prod`):**
16	- DB cluster `lobu-ai-prod-db` + pooler `lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler` + daily ScheduledBackup; backups to R2 serverName `lobu-ai-prod-db`.
17	- GitOps-managed at `packages/owletto/deploy/k8s/apps/lobu-db/` via its OWN Flux Kustomization `lobu-db` (separate path so it escapes the lobu app overlay's `summaries-` namePrefix → keeps the clean name). The lobu app overlay (`apps/lobu/overlays/summaries-prod`) no longer defines a DB; app+migrate `poolerService` point at `lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler` / `lobu-ai-prod-db-rw`.
18	- App DB creds secret `summaries-db-app` (NOT cluster-owned — survives cluster deletion). R2 creds `summaries-r2-backup-credentials` (SealedSecret).
19	
20	**Prevention shipped (lobu#989, merged `df38fbf4`):** `getTestDb()` refuses any DB whose name isn't test-shaped (`assertSafeTestDatabaseUrl`; override `LOBU_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TEST_DB=1`); baseline `00000000000000_baseline.sql` `migrate:down` is now `RAISE EXCEPTION` (was `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE`). owletto #208 (cutover) + #209 (GitOps codify) merged.
21	
22	**Querying prod (verified 2026-07-30).** The database is named **`owletto`** — not `lobu`, not `app`. `app` exists and is empty of app tables, so a wrong `-d` fails with a confusing `relation "runs" does not exist` rather than a missing-database error. The primary pod has two containers, so `-c postgres` is required:
23	
24	```
25	kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -c postgres -- \
26	  psql -U postgres -d owletto -A -F$'\t' -c "<sql>"
27	```
28	
29	Column names that do not exist and cost a retry each: `runs.updated_at` / `runs.approved_at` (the real ones are `created_at, completed_at, claimed_at, last_heartbeat_at, run_at, expires_at`), `entities.merged_into_id` (it is `merged_into`), `entity_identities.kind` (it is `namespace`). There is no `notifications` table.
30	
31	**PITR recovery runbook lessons (do these BEFORE cutover next time):** (1) PITR resets planner statistics → run `ANALYZE` or queries seq-scan and time out (`resolve_path` hit this). (2) A hand-made recovery cluster has NONE of the chart's tuning/resources — copy `shared_buffers`/`random_page_cost=1.1`/`effective_cache_size`/resources from the chart. (3) `geo_earthdistance` migration needs `cube`+`earthdistance` extensions pre-created as superuser (app role can't CREATE untrusted earthdistance) and conflicts with pre-squash `geo_lookup(p_lat,…)` (`DROP FUNCTION` it first). (4) CNPG `bootstrap` is immutable — a GitOps manifest adopting an existing recovered cluster MUST replicate its exact bootstrap or the webhook rejects the apply. (5) Flux `prune: true` on the apps Kustomization — removing a cluster from render deletes it; verify `kustomize build` before merge.

The lobu app overlay (`apps/lobu/overlays/summaries-prod`) no longer defines a DB; app+migrate `poolerService` point at `lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler` / `lobu-ai-prod-db-rw`.
- App DB creds secret `summaries-db-app` (NOT cluster-owned — survives cluster deletion). R2 creds `summaries-r2-backup-credentials` (SealedSecret).

**Prevention shipped (lobu#989, merged `df38fbf4`):** `getTestDb()` refuses any DB whose name isn't test-shaped (`assertSafeTestDatabaseUrl`; override `LOBU_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_TEST_DB=1`); baseline `00000000000000_baseline.sql` `migrate:down` is now `RAISE EXCEPTION` (was `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE`). owletto #208 (cutover) + #209 (GitOps codify) merged.

**Querying prod (verified 2026-07-30).** The database is named **`owletto`** — not `lobu`, not `app`. `app` exists and is empty of app tables, so a wrong `-d` fails with a confusing `relation "runs" does not exist` rather than a missing-database error. The primary pod has two containers, so `-c postgres` is required:

```
kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -c postgres -- \
  psql -U postgres -d owletto -A -F$'\t' -c "<sql>"
```

Column names that do not exist and cost a retry each: `runs.updated_at` / `runs.approved_at` (the real ones are `created_at, completed_at, claimed_at, last_heartbeat_at, run_at, expires_at`), `entities.merged_into_id` (it is `merged_into`), `entity_identities.kind` (it is `namespace`). There is no `notifications` table.

**PITR recovery runbook lessons (do these BEFORE cutover next time):** (1) PITR resets planner statistics → run `ANALYZE` or queries seq-scan and time out (`resolve_path` hit this). (2) A hand-made recovery cluster has NONE of the chart's tuning/resources — copy `shared_buffers`/`random_page_cost=1.1`/`effective_cache_size`/resources from the chart. (3) `geo_earthdistance` migration needs `cube`+`earthdistance` extensions pre-created as superuser (app role can't CREATE untrusted earthdistance) and conflicts with pre-squash `geo_lookup(p_lat,…)` (`DROP FUNCTION` it first). (4) CNPG `bootstrap` is immutable — a GitOps manifest adopting an existing recovered cluster MUST replicate its exact bootstrap or the webhook rejects the apply. (5) Flux `prune: true` on the apps Kustomization — removing a cluster from render deletes it; verify `kustomize build` before merge.

---
name: project_org_root_signin_guard
description: "#2358/owletto#646 MERGED: org root had no sign-in guard so a signed-out visitor saw the raw 401 body; prod-verify owed"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7ba1ff82-f964-4ade-8808-0ed38b90d913
  modified: 2026-07-30T14:20:26.177Z
---

lobu **#2358** (`e8b09ad9`) + owletto **#646** (`c4661c7a`), merged 2026-07-30. Prod-verify OWED — at merge time prod was still on `85bedf0f`.

**Bug:** `/$owner` was the ONLY owner-level route with no sign-in redirect, so `$owner.tsx` rendered `systemAgentError.message` verbatim — the raw server 401 "Authentication required. Use OAuth or API key." — as product copy. Its sibling `$owner/$.tsx` and `OwnerWorkspaceGate` each had their own guard; the root had none.

**Why it surfaced on a subdomain first:** `createSubdomainHistory` (`src/router.ts:31`) rewrites `/` → `/${owner}` *before* route matching, so on `{org}.lobu.ai` the `/` route — the only place that redirected a signed-out visitor at the bare root (`app/index.tsx`) — never matches. NOT subdomain-specific though: `app.lobu.ai/{owner}` reproduces identically.

**Why a route could ship with no guard:** the `/auth/login` search shape has 7 keys and TanStack's typed navigate/`<Link>` want all of them, so the literal was hand-copied at **7 call sites**, 5 of them purely writing `undefined`. Nothing to reuse — only a literal to copy. Fix added `src/lib/sign-in-redirect.ts` (`signInSearch`, `currentCallbackUrl`, `useAnonymousSignInRedirect`) and put the guard at the `$owner` layout (the chokepoint every `/{owner}/...` page passes through).

**Deliberate carve-outs, do not "simplify" away:**
- A 5xx/transport failure keeps rendering the error — an outage is not an authz problem. Tested.
- `useAnonymousSignInRedirect` skips when SSR injected a public bootstrap for that owner, so public orgs still render signed-out.
- `currentCallbackUrl()` reads `window.location`, NOT the router: on a subdomain the router is `/${owner}`-prefixed while the URL bar is not, so using the router would double-prefix the post-login bounce.

**Root cause of the original report was NOT this** — the user's browser session had gone stale (prod traffic was byte-for-byte identical to anonymous; `/api/auth/get-session` returned `200 null`). Re-login cleared it. This PR only fixes the *presentation* of that state.

Still open: [[project_public_workspace_rest_transport_gap]] (the authz half), and the bare `catch {}` in `multi-tenant.ts` that made ~87 prod 401s invisible in pod logs.

## Prod-verify gate (runnable cold — no prior session state needed)

```bash
git fetch -q origin
MERGE_SHA=e8b09ad9ff140c6fa6e10cfa4dda9489e1a9e259          # squash commit of #2358, NOT the branch head
DEPLOYED=$(curl -s https://app.lobu.ai/health | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['revision'])")
git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED" && echo "ROLLED OUT" || echo "not yet ($DEPLOYED)"
```

Argument order matters: merge commit FIRST. Reversed, it accepts a stale deploy.
Use `/health` `revision` — there is no `/version`. Gate on the squash commit; a squash
merge writes a new commit with no ancestry to the branch head, so the branch head exits 1 forever.

**Once it says ROLLED OUT, the actual check:** open `https://buremba.lobu.ai/` in a
signed-out/private window. Expected: redirect to `/auth/login?callbackUrl=...&intent=sign-in`.
Regression would be the old text "Couldn't load the workspace builder. / Authentication required.
Use OAuth or API key." Also spot-check a signed-in load still lands on the builder chat.

At merge time (2026-07-30 ~15:19 local) prod was on `85bedf0f` — NOT yet rolled out.

## What I found

Your prod backend is healthy — the failure is entirely in your browser's cookie jar.

**Server side is provably fine.** I pulled your newest session token straight from prod Postgres, signed it the way better-auth does (HMAC-SHA256, standard base64 — note `makeSignature` uses `btoa`, *not* base64url), and replayed it:

```
GET https://app.lobu.ai/api/auth/get-session
Cookie: __Secure-better-auth.session_token=<token>.<sig>
→ 200 {"session":{...},"user":{"email":"emrekabakci@gmail.com",...}}
```

Full session, correct user. So minting *and* validation both work.

**Everything else checks out too:**
- `user` row: verified, `principal_kind=human`, not banned
- 9 org memberships, `owner` on 7 (buremba, lobu-team, lobu-cloud, community, …)
- Cookie attrs from prod are correct: `Domain=.lobu.ai; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`
- Env is right: `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN=.lobu.ai`, `BASE_URL=https://app.lobu.ai`, `NODE_ENV=production`
- `resolveBaseUrl` is pinned by `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL`, so the host-independent `authCache` key (`packages/server/src/auth/index.tsx:87` — keyed on org only, not host) is inert here rather than a live bug
- Prod is up on `f77893a`, no auth errors in either pod's logs

**The tell:** 10 sessions minted for you since yesterday (6 today between 13:09 and 14:07 UTC, Chrome 151 / macOS). Every sign-in *succeeds* server-side — you just come back unauthenticated each time. That's the browser never presenting the cookie back, which is why it fails identically on Google, magic link, and Slack: they all share one cookie path.

The most likely cause is a stale host-only `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` on `app.lobu.ai` shadowing the newer `.lobu.ai` one — the browser sends both, better-auth reads the stale one, gets null, bounces you.

I couldn't confirm that directly because the Chrome extension isn't connected (`tabs_context_mcp` → "Browser extension is not connected"), and the pod logs redact the `cookie` header.

## Try this first

Clear cookies for `lobu.ai` (DevTools → Application → Cookies → both `app.lobu.ai` and `.lobu.ai`, delete all), then sign in again. If you want to confirm the diagnosis before clearing: open `https://app.lobu.ai/api/auth/get-session` in the tab where you *just* logged in — if it prints `null`, the cookie isn't reaching the server, and if the Application tab shows two `session_token` rows with different Domain values, that's the shadowing.

## Two unrelated things I noticed

- A duplicate account `emr.ekabakci@gmail.com` was created today at 00:53 UTC, with **no `account` rows at all** (magic-link user), and it auto-provisioned an org `emr-ekabakci`. Gmail ignores dots, so that's your inbox — likely a stray sign-in during your retries. Worth cleaning up, but tell me before I touch it.
- Your `user.phoneNumber` is `"burak-emre-kabakc-"` — a slug written into the phone column. Harmless today, but it's corrupt.

**Confidence:** high (90) that the server is not at fault — basis: I replayed a real signed session cookie against live prod and got a valid session back. Low (30) on the specific shadowed-cookie mechanism — basis: it fits every observation, but I never saw your actual cookie jar, so it's inference, not evidence.

**Next actions:**
1. Clear `lobu.ai` cookies and retry — fastest disambiguator, ~10 seconds.
2. Connect the Chrome extension and I'll finish the diagnosis properly by reading the real cookie jar and the bounce request chain.
3. Say the word and I'll delete the stray `emr.ekabakci@gmail.com` user + its `emr-ekabakci` org (one at a time, surfaced for confirmation per the org-deletion rule).
4. Separately worth fixing: `authCache` keyed on `organizationId` only while `baseURL` is request-derived — safe today only because `PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL` is set, which is a silent dependency.

# Browser-driven verification (authenticated)

For any UI verification that needs a signed-in session (past the auth wall), mint a session cookie from the DB and drive the **paired Owletto extension** through the Lobu connector-operations bridge (`lobu call manage_operations`, or the SDK `operations` namespace). This runs in the user's real logged-in Chrome — no separate headless browser, no CDP, no extra browser tooling to install.

## Scope

The forged session cookie authenticates the **web admin REST mounted at `/`** (`/api/auth/*`, `/api/<orgSlug>/...`, the SPA — anything `lobu apply` and the web app talk to). It does **NOT** authenticate the **public Agent API at `/lobu`** (`/lobu/api/v1/agents/*`, `/lobu/api/v1/agents/<id>/sessions`) — that path expects a JWT bearer from the OAuth device flow (`lobu login`) or a PAT. If `/lobu/api/v1/agents` returns `401` despite a valid cookie, switch to `lobu chat` / `lobu token`.

## Pick a target

Local dev backend (with prod DB attached over Tailscale): `https://<your-tailscale-host>.ts.net:8443`. Prod: `https://app.lobu.ai`.

## Grab the secret + session token

```bash
# Local dev backend uses .env's BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
SECRET=$(grep '^BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)

# Prod uses the secret on the K8s pod
SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod \
  $(kubectl get pod -n summaries-prod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=lobu-app -o name | head -1 | sed 's|pod/||') \
  -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET)
```

Session token from the DB. With no local `DATABASE_URL` set, exec psql inside the prod DB pod (the prod DB serves both targets):

```bash
DBURL=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod <lobu-app-pod> -- printenv DATABASE_URL)
PGPASS=$(printf '%s' "$DBURL" | sed -E 's#.*://[^:]+:([^@]+)@.*#\1#')
TOKEN=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -- \
  env PGPASSWORD="REDACTED" psql -h lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler -U summaries -d owletto -tAc \
  "SELECT token FROM session WHERE \"userId\" = '<user_id>' AND \"expiresAt\" > NOW() ORDER BY \"updatedAt\" DESC LIMIT 1")
```

## Sign the cookie

better-auth uses HMAC-SHA256, base64, then URL-encode — base64**url** does *not* validate.

```bash

  const {createHmac}=require("node:crypto");
  const sig=createHmac("sha256",process.env.SECRET).update(process.env.TOKEN).digest("base64");
  console.log(encodeURIComponent(`${process.env.TOKEN}.${sig}`));
')
```

Cookie name is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` whenever the baseURL is `https://` (prod and Tailscale dev qualify; only plain-http localhost uses the unprefixed `better-auth.session_token`).

## Find the Chrome connection

Browser actions dispatch to a paired Chrome extension connection (usually org `buremba`):

```bash
lobu call manage_connections --org buremba --arg action=list --raw
```

Pick the `chrome` connector with `status: active` on the machine whose browser you want to drive. `operations.listAvailable({ connection_id })` reports per-target `readiness` and `execution_targets` — use it to check the device is actually online before a long verification.

  });

2	name: reference_scrape_pin_is_not_the_human_browser
3	description: "A connection's device_worker_id means 'scrape with this browser' and drives EVERY chrome action it dispatches — so interactive staging actions (x.prepare_reply, linkedin.prepare_comment) open their tab on the cron machine, where the human never sees it"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory

8	  modified: 2026-08-02T22:15:33.844Z
9	---
10	
11	`dispatchChromeActionToExtension` routes every chrome action through
12	`preferredBrowserWorkerForConnection(parentConnectionId)` — the parent connection's
13	`device_worker_id`. That pin means **"scrape with this browser"**, and for a sync it is
14	right: the timeline scrape belongs on the always-on machine.
15	
16	It is wrong for an **interactive** action. `x.prepare_reply` and `linkedin.prepare_comment`
17	exist to put a page in front of a person. Honouring the scrape pin stages the draft on
18	whichever box runs the cron, so the human never sees it.
19	
20	Burak's org, 2026-08-02 — both content connections pinned to the Mac mini:
21	
22	| connection | connector | device_worker | machine |
23	|---|---|---|---|
24	| 369 `chrome` | chrome | `2e8a0557` | Mac mini |
25	| 399 `x-twitter-bu7emba` | x | `2e8a0557` | Mac mini |
26	| 412 `linkedin-buremba` | linkedin | `2e8a0557` | Mac mini |
27	| 432 `chrome-macbook` | chrome | `709f0d3a` | MacBook |
28	
29	He works on the MacBook. Every staged draft landed on the Mac mini: *"where is it i can't
30	see it."* The action reported `completed` with `prepared: true` every time — **a successful
31	run is not evidence the human can see the result.**
32	
33	## Telling the machines apart from a run output
34	
35	`tab_id` ranges differ per browser: Mac mini tabs were `1949…`, MacBook tabs `5585…`. Quick
36	sanity check that a staged tab is where you think it is.
37	
38	## The fix (coded, needs deploy)
39	
40	Reserved input key `target_browser_connection_id`, consumed and stripped server-side in
41	`dispatch-chrome-action.ts`, resolving that chrome connection's worker as
42	`preferredDeviceWorkerId`. Fails closed — an unresolvable target errors rather than quietly
43	staging on the scrape machine. The connector stamps it at its dispatch chokepoint from
44	`input.browser_connection_id` ?? `config.interactive_browser_connection_id`. **No wire or IPC
45	change was needed**: `action_input` already flows verbatim connector → IPC → POST → handler,
46	and the server already mutates that bag (`holder_run_id`).
47	
48	Why the connector decides and not the server: only the connector knows an action is
49	interactive. `run_type = 'action'` is *nearly* the right seam but not all actions are
50	interactive, and "which browser is the human at" has no reliable signal — both Chromes
51	heartbeat continuously, so freshest-`last_seen_at` is a coin flip. Explicit beats guessed.
52	
53	## Interim lever until it deploys
54	
55	There is no SDK method documented for repinning, but **`client.connections.update` accepts an
56	undocumented `device_worker_id`** and it works:
57	
58	```js
59	await client.connections.update({ connection_id: 399, device_worker_id: '<uuid>' });
60	```
61	
62	Tradeoff: this moves the *scrape* too. End state once deployed — restore the pin to the
63	always-on Mac mini and set `config.interactive_browser_connection_id = 432`.

66	[[reference_connector_actions_live_in_the_db]], [[reference_x_ignores_intent_text_param]].

`dispatchChromeActionToExtension` routes every chrome action through
`preferredBrowserWorkerForConnection(parentConnectionId)` — the parent connection's
`device_worker_id`. That pin means **"scrape with this browser"**, and for a sync it is
right: the timeline scrape belongs on the always-on machine.

It is wrong for an **interactive** action. `x.prepare_reply` and `linkedin.prepare_comment`
exist to put a page in front of a person. Honouring the scrape pin stages the draft on
whichever box runs the cron, so the human never sees it.

Burak's org, 2026-08-02 — both content connections pinned to the Mac mini:

| connection | connector | device_worker | machine |
|---|---|---|---|
| 369 `chrome` | chrome | `2e8a0557` | Mac mini |
| 399 `x-twitter-bu7emba` | x | `2e8a0557` | Mac mini |
| 412 `linkedin-buremba` | linkedin | `2e8a0557` | Mac mini |
| 432 `chrome-macbook` | chrome | `709f0d3a` | MacBook |

He works on the MacBook. Every staged draft landed on the Mac mini: *"where is it i can't
see it."* The action reported `completed` with `prepared: true` every time — **a successful
run is not evidence the human can see the result.**

## Telling the machines apart from a run output

`tab_id` ranges differ per browser: Mac mini tabs were `1949…`, MacBook tabs `5585…`. Quick
sanity check that a staged tab is where you think it is.

## The fix (coded, needs deploy)

Reserved input key `target_browser_connection_id`, consumed and stripped server-side in
`dispatch-chrome-action.ts`, resolving that chrome connection's worker as
`preferredDeviceWorkerId`. Fails closed — an unresolvable target errors rather than quietly
staging on the scrape machine. The connector stamps it at its dispatch chokepoint from
`input.browser_connection_id` ?? `config.interactive_browser_connection_id`. **No wire or IPC
change was needed**: `action_input` already flows verbatim connector → IPC → POST → handler,
and the server already mutates that bag (`holder_run_id`).

Why the connector decides and not the server: only the connector knows an action is
interactive. `run_type = 'action'` is *nearly* the right seam but not all actions are
interactive, and "which browser is the human at" has no reliable signal — both Chromes
heartbeat continuously, so freshest-`last_seen_at` is a coin flip. Explicit beats guessed.

## Interim lever until it deploys

There is no SDK method documented for repinning, but **`client.connections.update` accepts an
undocumented `device_worker_id`** and it works:

```js
await client.connections.update({ connection_id: 399, device_worker_id: '<uuid>' });
```

Tradeoff: this moves the *scrape* too. End state once deployed — restore the pin to the
always-on Mac mini and set `config.interactive_browser_connection_id = 432`.

Related: [[reference_x_handle_is_bu7emba_not_buremba]] (the two-Chrome table),
[[reference_connector_actions_live_in_the_db]], [[reference_x_ignores_intent_text_param]].

**Root cause found.** Look at `before`:

```json
{"href":"https://app.lobu.ai/auth/login","len":116,
 "names":["__Secure-better-auth.session_token"]}
```

That cookie is **readable from `document.cookie`** — so it is *not* HttpOnly. But prod always sets that cookie `HttpOnly` (we saw the `Set-Cookie` header). So this one was never set by better-auth — it was written by JavaScript. And after planting a known-good signed cookie, `get-session` *still* returned `null`, i.e. the stale one is winning.

That's a leftover forged cookie from a previous browser-verification session — exactly the `document.cookie='__Secure-better-auth.session_token=…'` recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. It's non-HttpOnly and permanently shadows every real login. Let me confirm the scopes and clear it.

---
name: reference_forged_session_cookie_shadows_real_logins
description: "A leftover document.cookie-planted session cookie (non-HttpOnly, host-only) shadows EVERY real login on that machine — the BROWSER_TESTING.md recipe leaves this trap behind"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

2026-08-06: `emrekabakci@gmail.com` could not log in to `app.lobu.ai` on **any** method
(Google, magic link, Slack). Every attempt bounced back to `/auth/login`.

**Not a server bug.** Sessions were being minted correctly — 10 rows in `session` in 24h —
and the server validated them fine. The break was entirely in the browser cookie jar.

**Root cause:** the jar held `__Secure-better-auth.session_token = 73qCtIYuVIGv…` (81 chars)
that was **readable from `document.cookie`**, i.e. NOT HttpOnly. better-auth always sets that
cookie `HttpOnly` (verified on the live `Set-Cookie`), so this one was never server-set — it
was planted by JavaScript, a leftover from a previous browser-verification session using the
`document.cookie='__Secure-better-auth.session_token=…'` recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`.
Its token had **no row in `session`** — a dead session.

**Why re-logging-in never fixed it:** the real login sets the cookie on `Domain=.lobu.ai`,
while the planted one was host-only on `app.lobu.ai`. They coexist as two distinct cookies
with the same name, so the browser sends both. Verified with curl that **duplicates fail in
either order** — `stale; good` and `good; stale` both return `null`. So one stale planted
cookie permanently bricks logins on that machine until it is manually cleared.

**Fix:** expire the name across every scope from JS (it is not HttpOnly, so JS *can* delete
it), then log in normally:
```js
for (const d of ['','; domain=app.lobu.ai','; domain=.lobu.ai','; domain=lobu.ai'])
  document.cookie = '__Secure-better-auth.session_token=; max-age=0; path=/'+d+'; secure; samesite=lax';
```

**Process fix owed:** `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` should tell you to clear the planted cookie
when the verification finishes, or to drive a throwaway Chrome profile. As written, every
authenticated UI verification leaves a login-bricking landmine in the human's real browser.

Diagnosis path that worked, without the claude-in-chrome extension: drive the paired Owletto
extension (`client.operations.execute`, chrome connection **479** = MacBook / worker
`709f0d3a`; 432 = Mac mini) and `evaluate` `document.cookie` + `fetch('/api/auth/get-session')`.
Note `evaluate` returns its value at `output.value`, not `output.result.value`, and
`network_intercept_*` needs `patterns` on start and `session_id` on drain/stop — and it
returns **response bodies only**, never request headers, so it cannot show you a `Cookie` header.

Related: [[reference_scrape_pin_is_not_the_human_browser]] (479 vs 432),
[[feedback_kubectl_printenv_can_silently_return_empty]].

---
name: feedback_kubectl_printenv_can_silently_return_empty
description: "kubectl exec -- printenv X with stderr suppressed returns EMPTY when the pod is gone, and an empty-key HMAC then fabricates a convincing 'the secret rotated' conclusion"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

2026-08-06, debugging a prod login failure, I concluded "`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is regenerated
on every deploy" — stated confidently, with two differing signatures as evidence. **It was
false.** The sealed secret had not changed since 2026-06-22 and both replicas agreed.

**What actually happened:** prod rolled mid-session, so
`SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n ns "$OLD_POD" -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET 2>/dev/null)` hit a pod
that no longer existed. `2>/dev/null` ate the error, the assignment succeeded with an **empty
string**, and `openssl dgst -hmac ""` / `createHmac("sha256","")` happily produced a signature.
Comparing that empty-key signature against a real one looked exactly like a rotated secret.

Proof it was empty-key, and the check that should have run first:
```
HMAC("",  REDACTED) = REDACTED  # my "old" sig
HMAC(key, REDACTED) = REDACTED  # real
```

**Why:** an empty key is a *valid* input to every HMAC implementation. Nothing errors. The
failure is silent all the way to a wrong root-cause claim.

**How to apply:** never feed a shell-captured secret/token into crypto without asserting its
length first, and do not suppress stderr on the read.
```bash
SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n ns "$POD" -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET | tr -d '\r\n')
[ ${#SECRET} -eq 44 ] || { echo "BAD SECRET READ len=${#SECRET}"; exit 1; }
```
Re-resolve the pod name on every command when a rollout may be in flight — a pod name captured
minutes ago is not stable. More generally: when a measurement suddenly flips to "broken",
suspect the measurement before announcing a root cause, and prefer a `set -e` + length-assert
script over a chain of `$(...)` captures.

Related: [[feedback_verify_dont_reason_from_construction]],
[[feedback_piped_make_exit_code_is_a_false_green]],
[[reference_forged_session_cookie_shadows_real_logins]].

content.text:
Yes — the Owletto extension worked (claude-in-chrome was the wrong bridge). **You're logged in now**, and I found the actual cause.

## Root cause

Your browser held a `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` cookie that was **readable from `document.cookie`** — so not HttpOnly. Prod always sets that cookie `HttpOnly` (confirmed on the live `Set-Cookie`), so it was never server-set. It was planted by JavaScript: a leftover from a previous authenticated UI verification using the `document.cookie='__Secure-better-auth.session_token=…'` recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`.

Its token (`73qCtIYuVIGv…`) has **no row in the `session` table** — a dead session.

Why logging in never fixed it: a real login sets the cookie on `Domain=.lobu.ai`, while the planted one was host-only on `app.lobu.ai`. Two distinct cookies, same name, both sent. I confirmed with curl that duplicates fail **in either order** — `stale; good` and `good; stale` both return `null`. So that one stale cookie bricked every login attempt on this machine, on every auth method, indefinitely.

## Evidence

- Server side is healthy: your session validated end-to-end once signed correctly
- In your Chrome, `/api/auth/get-session` → `null` while you sat on `/auth/login`
- Cleared the stale cookie, planted a correctly signed one → `https://app.lobu.ai/buremba/activity`

## Correction

Partway through I told you `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` rotates on every deploy. That was wrong, and it was my own measurement error — prod rolled mid-session, my `kubectl exec … printenv 2>/dev/null` hit a dead pod and returned an **empty string**, and `HMAC("", token)` produced a perfectly valid-looking signature. I verified it: the "old" signature is exactly the empty-key HMAC. The secret is stable (unchanged since June, both replicas agree).

## One thing you should do

The cookie I planted carries a real session (from your own 14:07 Google login) but was set via JS, so it's **not HttpOnly** — the token is exposed to JavaScript on `app.lobu.ai`. Sign out and sign in normally once; that replaces it with a proper HttpOnly cookie.

## Also found (unrelated)

- Duplicate account `emr.ekabakci@gmail.com`, created today 00:53 UTC with **no `account` rows**, plus an auto-provisioned org `emr-ekabakci`. Gmail ignores dots, so it's your inbox — likely a stray magic-link during the retries.
- `user.phoneNumber` on your row is `"burak-emre-kabakc-"` — a slug in the phone column.

**Confidence:** high (92) on root cause — basis: reproduced the null in your real browser, identified the non-HttpOnly dead-token cookie, proved duplicates fail both orders via curl, and restored access by clearing it. Medium (60) on *how* the cookie got there — it matches the BROWSER_TESTING recipe exactly, but I have no log proving which session planted it.

**Next actions:**
1. Sign out / sign in fresh to get an HttpOnly cookie back (recommended, ~30s).
2. Fix `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` — the recipe leaves a login-bricking cookie in your real browser; it should mandate clearing it afterward or using a throwaway profile. I can do this as a small PR.
3. Say the word and I'll delete the stray `emr.ekabakci@gmail.com` user + `emr-ekabakci` org (surfaced one at a time per the org-deletion rule).
4. Worth considering: better-auth silently returns `null` on duplicate cookies. A one-line warn when the `Cookie` header carries two `session_token` entries would have made this obvious in minutes.

set -e
P=$(kubectl get pods -n summaries-prod --no-headers | awk '/lobu-app/{print $1; exit}')

GOOD_T="REDACTED"

DEAD_T="ZZZZdeadsession000000000000000ZZ"

N="__Secure-better-auth.session_token"
r(){ curl -s -m 15 https://app.lobu.ai/api/auth/get-session -H "Cookie: $1" | head -c 60; echo; }
echo -n "good only        : "; r "$N=$GOOD"
echo -n "dead only        : "; r "$N=$DEAD"
echo -n "dead; good       : "; r "$N=$DEAD; $N=$GOOD"

content.text:
## The defect, stated precisely

Two cookies can exist with the same name at different scopes — host-only `app.lobu.ai` and `Domain=.lobu.ai`. The browser sends both, the server takes the **first**, and RFC 6265 §5.4 orders equal-path cookies **oldest first**. So once a stale host-only cookie exists, every future login writes a *newer* cookie that is structurally incapable of winning. Login is permanently unrecoverable from inside the app — clearing cookies by hand is the only escape.

The bad cookie came from the BROWSER_TESTING recipe in your case, but that's the instance. The class is: **nothing in the sign-in path makes a fresh login authoritative over an older cookie at a different scope.** Any host-only leftover does this — including one the server itself set during any window when `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` was unset (local dev, or prod before it was configured).

## The proper fix

**1. Converge the cookie scope at sign-in.** Wherever better-auth emits the session cookie with `Domain=.lobu.ai`, the same response must also emit a host-only deletion of that name:

```
Set-Cookie: __Secure-better-auth.session_token=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=Lax
```

No `Domain` attribute → targets the host-only twin specifically. A login then deterministically converges to exactly one cookie. This belongs in a response middleware in the gateway that inspects outgoing `Set-Cookie` headers — that's the chokepoint every method (Google, Slack, magic link, credential, passkey) already funnels through, so it fixes the class in one place rather than per-provider.

It must cover the other domain-scoped better-auth cookies too — `.state` and `.pkce_code_verifier` shadow identically, and a shadowed `state` breaks the OAuth callback rather than the session.

**2. Self-heal on unresolvable.** When a presented session cookie resolves to no session, expire the **host-only** scope. Gate it on `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` being set (in local dev the host-only cookie is the real one). This is safe by construction: if the domain-scoped cookie had been the winner it would have resolved, so the only thing being deleted is the thing that's already dead. It repairs already-bricked browsers on their next request, without anyone re-logging-in.

**3. Make it visible.** Warn when the inbound `Cookie` header carries more than one entry for the session cookie name. That single log line is the difference between this taking five minutes and taking an hour — right now the failure is completely silent, and it compounds with the bare `catch {}` in `multi-tenant.ts` you already have noted as hiding ~87 prod 401s.

**4. Stop the source.** `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` plants a **non-HttpOnly** cookie into your real browser with no teardown. It should use a throwaway profile, or mandate expiring the cookie at the end of the verification. As written, every authenticated UI verification leaves a login-bricking landmine behind.

## What I'd skip

- `__Host-` prefix would make duplicates structurally impossible, but it forbids `Domain` — you'd lose session sharing across `{org}.lobu.ai`. Not viable.
- Bumping `cookiePrefix` would unbrick every affected user in one shot (a new name can't be shadowed by the old), but it logs everyone out and doesn't prevent recurrence. Only worth it if #2 shows real users are stuck.

I'd ship 1 + 3 together, then 2, with 4 as the process fix. Fix 2 is what tells you whether real users were hit — right now that's unknowable, since the evidence lives only in client cookie jars.

**Confidence:** high (90) on the mechanism — basis: first-wins precedence measured directly against prod just now with a correctly-signed secret (`dead; good` → null, `good; dead` → session), plus RFC ordering. Medium (55) that real non-agent users are affected — basis: only 3 users have had sessions in 2 days, which is suggestive but not evidence, and I have no way to inspect other people's cookie jars.

**Next actions:**
1. I can implement 1 + 3 in a worktree with a red→green test — a reproducer asserting `dead; good` resolves the session after the fix.
2. Add 2 as the self-heal in the same PR or a follow-up.
3. Patch `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` — smallest change, stops new landmines immediately.
4. Decide on the `cookiePrefix` bump once 3 is live and you can see whether duplicate-cookie warnings are showing up for other users.

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **`events.id` is a stored-version id, not stable source identity.** Connector resyncs can supersede a row and allocate a new id for the same source item. Cross-sync identity and dedupe must use the connector's stable `origin_id` (scoped to its connection/source) or an explicit domain key, never `events.id`.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Mutation checks require proof that the mutation landed: assert the old pattern exists, verify a countable source change, and confirm the focused test fails before restoring the fix and rerunning green. A green test after a no-op mutation proves nothing.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- **A UI change owes visual proof.** For an Owletto pointer PR, `make ui-review` publishes the before/after comparison on the exact merged Owletto PR and links it from the parent. Publishing the proof is what the gate asserts — review it like any other change on the PR. A changed pointer republishes it.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. `make ui-review`. It passes non-Owletto changes as not applicable. For an Owletto pointer change, run `ARTIFACT=<hosted-html-url> make ui-review`; it publishes the before/after proof on the exact merged Owletto PR, links it from the parent, and passes. No `ARTIFACT` means no proof and no pass.
10. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
11. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Never introduce a new table or change the database design, API surface, or SDK surface without explicitly surfacing the proposal and receiving user confirmation first.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and pass that URL as `ARTIFACT` to `make ui-review`. The gate records it on the Owletto PR and binds human approval to the exact parent-base and Owletto-pointer pair.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.

History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.

+### Always expire the planted cookie (step 5 is not optional)
+`document.cookie` writes a **host-only** cookie (`app.lobu.ai`), while a real sign-in writes
+the same name at `Domain=.lobu.ai`. Both then live in the jar, the browser sends both, and the
+server resolves whichever comes **first** — which RFC 6265 §5.4 makes the **oldest**. So a
+leftover planted cookie outranks every subsequent real login, and once its session expires the
+human is locked out of `app.lobu.ai` with no in-app way to recover: each new sign-in mints a
+strictly newer cookie that can never win. This cost a full debugging session on 2026-08-06.
+The server now expires the host-only twin whenever it sets a domain-scoped auth cookie
+(`auth/session-cookie-scope.ts`), so a fresh sign-in self-heals a poisoned jar — but do not
+lean on that. Expire what you planted.

## Summary

- A session cookie can exist at two scopes at once — host-only (`app.lobu.ai`) and domain-scoped (`Domain=.lobu.ai`). The browser sends **both**, we resolve the **first**, and RFC 6265 §5.4 orders equal-path cookies **oldest-first**. A stale host-only twin is therefore unbeatable: every later sign-in writes a strictly newer cookie that can never win, so the user is locked out with **no in-app way to recover** — re-logging-in provably cannot fix it.
- `/exchange-token` and `/local-init` were manufacturing exactly that twin in production: `mintSessionCookieValue` set the cookie **host-only** while Better Auth sets it `Domain=$AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`. `document.cookie` planting per `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` produces the same thing.
- Fix makes sign-in authoritative: whenever a response sets a domain-scoped auth cookie, it also expires the host-only twin of that name. Applied at the `/api/auth/*` chokepoint it covers Google, Slack, magic link, credential and passkey in one place — plus `state`/`pkce_code_verifier`, where a shadowed value breaks the OAuth callback rather than the session. This also **self-heals an already-bricked browser** on its next sign-in.

Measured against prod (`/api/auth/get-session`, correctly signed cookie, 2026-08-06):

| `Cookie` header | Result |
|---|---|
| `good` | session |
| `dead` | `null` |
| `dead; good` | `null` ← the brick |
| `good; dead` | session |

Also adds a `logger.warn` when one request carries the same session cookie name more than once. That state was previously **completely silent** — `get-session` just answers `200 null` forever — which is what made this cost a full debugging session.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: `make test-unit` (exit 0), targeted `bunx vitest run src/auth/__tests__/exchange-token-cookie.test.ts` (11/11)
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot behavior: ran `./scripts/test-bot.sh` or relevant eval — n/a

### red → green

New unit suite, before `src/auth/session-cookie-scope.ts` existed:

```
error: Cannot find module '../../auth/session-cookie-scope'
 0 pass
 1 fail
```

After:

```
 8 pass
 0 fail
 22 expect() calls
```

Wiring test, mutated (`Domain` push removed from `mintSessionCookieValue`) — proof the assertion is load-bearing and not vacuously green:

```
 × deep-link token exchange > GET /exchange-token scopes the cookie to the zone and expires the host-only twin
   → expected 'better-auth.session_token=HmSFPk4qzzi…' to contain 'Domain=.lobu.ai'
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)
```

Restored:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

## Notes

Found while diagnosing a real lockout: `emrekabakci@gmail.com` could not sign in to `app.lobu.ai` on **any** method for hours. Sessions were being minted correctly the whole time (10 rows in `session` in 24h) and the server validated them fine — the jar held a dead host-only `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` whose token had no row in `session`, and it outranked every new login.

Deliberate carve-outs, please don't "simplify" them away:
- `convergeSetCookieScope` **no-ops when no cookie zone is configured**. In local dev the host-only cookie IS the real session cookie; expiring it would log the developer out on every sign-in.
- The expiry header carries **no `Domain`** on purpose — deletion matches on (name, domain, path), so omitting it targets the twin and leaves the real cookie alone.
- The expiry keeps `Secure` even though it is a deletion: browsers reject any `Set-Cookie` for a `__Secure-`-prefixed name that lacks it, so without it the deletion silently no-ops.
- A `Set-Cookie` that is already an expiry is skipped, so sign-out is untouched.

`docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` now makes expiring the planted cookie a mandatory step — as written, every authenticated UI verification left a login-bricking cookie in the human's real browser.

Not included, deliberately: a delete-on-unresolvable path. Once sign-in converges the scope, a bricked browser heals on its next sign-in without one, and deleting cookies on an unauthenticated request is a materially riskier change for no additional coverage.

review:
	@./scripts/review.sh $(if $(BASE),--base $(BASE),)

# Pre-review fixer: the reviewer CLI with WRITE access + the review rubrics,
# fixing review-grade findings (bugs, slop, stale claims) in the working tree
# BEFORE `make review` posts a status. Posts nothing, commits nothing —
# inspect its diff, commit, then run `make review` once on the settled HEAD.
review-fix:
	@./scripts/review-fix.sh $(if $(BASE),--base $(BASE),)

# Visual counterpart to `make review`: non-Owletto PRs pass as not applicable.
# Pointer PRs post/update proof on the exact merged Owletto PR, link it from
# this Lobu PR, and attach a passing `ui-review` status. Publishing the proof is
# what the gate asserts, so no ARTIFACT means no proof and no pass. ARTIFACT and
# OPEN are read directly by scripts/ui-review.ts, avoiding shell interpolation
# of URLs.
ui-review:
	@bun scripts/ui-review.ts

# Fast, deterministic CI gates that need NO database — the exact checks that
# `make review` (LLM-verdict only) does NOT run. Run this before opening/updating
# a PR so knip / typecheck / lint failures don't surface only in CI.
# NOT a substitute for the DB-backed suites (make test-integration) when you
# touch server/runtime code — but it catches the cheap, common misses.

---
name: reference-review-harness-claude-needs-foreground
description: "REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review fails with a bare \"Execution error\" as a background task, so run it in the foreground — but as of 2026-08-02 claude is Fable-5 quota-blocked and CODEX is the working reviewer, the reverse of what this note used to say"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 82368b87-6555-4432-bce4-6459714348f7
  modified: 2026-08-05T11:47:44.034Z
---

`REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` **must run in the foreground**. Launched as a
background task it dies at the `>> invoking claude review` line, and the
preserved inline output is exactly 15 bytes: `Execution error`. Three
consecutive attempts on PR #2399 failed identically; the same command run
synchronously in the foreground succeeded immediately (verdict 92/88).

The failure is silent-ish and looks like an external kill, so it invites
re-running the same thing. Check
`/tmp/lobu-review-claude-inline.*` — a 15-byte `Execution error` file is the
signature.

## REVERSED 2026-08-02: claude is the blocked one, codex works

This note used to say codex was quota-blocked until Aug 5 and foreground claude was
the only path. That flipped. On PR #2437:

- `REVIEWER_CLI=claude` fails **immediately**, both for `make review-fix` and
  `make review`, with `You've reached your Fable 5 limit.` The claude reviewer is
  backed by Fable 5, so a Fable quota exhausts it. `make review` **fails closed** and
  explicitly refuses to fall back: "The review gate fails closed and will not fall
  back to another reviewer."
- `REVIEWER_CLI=codex` runs fine — it just takes **longer than 600s**, so a
  foreground Bash call times out and gets backgrounded. Codex tolerates background
  execution (only claude has the `Execution error` problem), so backgrounding it is
  correct, not a workaround.

**Do not trust a recorded reviewer-availability window.** Both reviewers are quota-
gated on separate budgets that move independently; the only way to know which works
is to try one.

## FLIPPED BACK 2026-08-05: codex blocked, foreground claude works

On PR #2499, `make review` (default `auto` → codex) failed with
`ERROR: You've hit your usage limit. ... try again at Aug 10th, 2026 1:53 AM`
and `make: *** [review] Error 1`. `REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` **in the
foreground** then succeeded on the first try (verdict bug_free 80, 0 blockers)
and posted the `pi-review` status normally.

So within three days the working reviewer flipped codex→claude→codex→claude. The
foreground rule for claude still holds. Budget ~20 min of foreground wall-clock.

`scripts/review.sh` supports only `codex|claude`.

Related: [[reference_review_harness_quota_and_schema_traps]],
[[project_review_harness_codex_single_point]], [[feedback_run_review_without_asking]]

**Fallback accounts are NOT a fallback (2026-08-05):** when the primary `codex` hits its
usage limit, `REVIEWER_CLI=pi PI_REVIEW_PROVIDER=openai-codex-2` (and `-3`) both die with
`OAuth refresh failed for openai-codex-N` — the refresh tokens are expired and only a human
re-login fixes it. Don't burn round-trips cycling accounts; go straight to
`REVIEWER_CLI=claude`. See [[project_provider_quota_park_and_health]].

2026-08-06: `emrekabakci@gmail.com` could not log in to `app.lobu.ai` on **any** method
(Google, magic link, Slack). Every attempt bounced back to `/auth/login`.

**Not a server bug.** Sessions were being minted correctly — 10 rows in `session` in 24h —
and the server validated them fine. The break was entirely in the browser cookie jar.

**Root cause:** the jar held `__Secure-better-auth.session_token = 73qCtIYuVIGv…` (81 chars)
that was **readable from `document.cookie`**, i.e. NOT HttpOnly. better-auth always sets that
cookie `HttpOnly` (verified on the live `Set-Cookie`), so this one was never server-set — it
was planted by JavaScript, a leftover from a previous browser-verification session using the
`document.cookie='__Secure-better-auth.session_token=…'` recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`.
Its token had **no row in `session`** — a dead session.

**Why re-logging-in never fixed it:** the real login sets the cookie on `Domain=.lobu.ai`,
while the planted one was host-only on `app.lobu.ai`. They coexist as two distinct cookies
with the same name, so the browser sends both. Verified with curl that **duplicates fail in
either order** — `stale; good` and `good; stale` both return `null`. So one stale planted
cookie permanently bricks logins on that machine until it is manually cleared.

**Fix:** expire the name across every scope from JS (it is not HttpOnly, so JS *can* delete
it), then log in normally:
```js
for (const d of ['','; domain=app.lobu.ai','; domain=.lobu.ai','; domain=lobu.ai'])
  document.cookie = '__Secure-better-auth.session_token=; max-age=0; path=/'+d+'; secure; samesite=lax';
```

**Process fix owed:** `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` should tell you to clear the planted cookie
when the verification finishes, or to drive a throwaway Chrome profile. As written, every
authenticated UI verification leaves a login-bricking landmine in the human's real browser.

Diagnosis path that worked, without the claude-in-chrome extension: drive the paired Owletto
extension (`client.operations.execute`, chrome connection **479** = MacBook / worker
`709f0d3a`; 432 = Mac mini) and `evaluate` `document.cookie` + `fetch('/api/auth/get-session')`.
Note `evaluate` returns its value at `output.value`, not `output.result.value`, and
`network_intercept_*` needs `patterns` on start and `session_id` on drain/stop — and it
returns **response bodies only**, never request headers, so it cannot show you a `Cookie` header.

Related: [[reference_scrape_pin_is_not_the_human_browser]] (479 vs 432),
[[feedback_kubectl_printenv_can_silently_return_empty]].

---
name: reference_forged_session_cookie_shadows_real_logins
description: "A host-only session cookie outranks the domain-scoped one forever (RFC 6265 oldest-first + we resolve the first), permanently bricking login — FIXED by PR #2558, prod-verify owed"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 3c1aa6f1-c607-4eb1-9112-65ea2a8588c2
  modified: 2026-08-06T16:08:01.720Z
---

2026-08-06: `emrekabakci@gmail.com` could not log in to `app.lobu.ai` on **any** method
(Google, magic link, Slack). Every attempt bounced back to `/auth/login`.

**Not a server bug.** Sessions were being minted correctly — 10 rows in `session` in 24h —
and the server validated them fine. The break was entirely in the browser cookie jar.

**Root cause:** the jar held `__Secure-better-auth.session_token = 73qCtIYuVIGv…` (81 chars)
that was **readable from `document.cookie`**, i.e. NOT HttpOnly. better-auth always sets that
cookie `HttpOnly` (verified on the live `Set-Cookie`), so this one was never server-set — it
was planted by JavaScript, a leftover from a previous browser-verification session using the
`document.cookie='__Secure-better-auth.session_token=…'` recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`.
Its token had **no row in `session`** — a dead session.

**Why re-logging-in never fixed it:** the real login sets the cookie on `Domain=.lobu.ai`,
while the planted one was host-only on `app.lobu.ai`. They coexist as two distinct cookies
with the same name, so the browser sends both. Verified with curl that **duplicates fail in
either order** — `stale; good` and `good; stale` both return `null`. So one stale planted
cookie permanently bricks logins on that machine until it is manually cleared.

**Fix:** expire the name across every scope from JS (it is not HttpOnly, so JS *can* delete
it), then log in normally:
```js
for (const d of ['','; domain=app.lobu.ai','; domain=.lobu.ai','; domain=lobu.ai'])
  document.cookie = '__Secure-better-auth.session_token=; max-age=0; path=/'+d+'; secure; samesite=lax';
```

## FIXED — PR #2558 (`fix(server): converge session-cookie scope…`)

The planted cookie was only ONE source. The production source was
`mintSessionCookieValue` (`auth/routes.ts`): it set the session cookie **host-only** while
Better Auth sets it `Domain=$AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`, so `/exchange-token` and `/local-init`
(CLI / macOS menu bar deep links) manufactured the same brick for real users.

Shipped, one PR: (1) `auth/session-cookie-scope.ts` — whenever a response sets a
domain-scoped auth cookie, also emit a host-only expiry of that name, wired at the
`/api/auth/*` chokepoint so it covers every method at once **plus** `state`/`pkce_code_verifier`
(a shadowed `state` breaks the OAuth callback, not the session); (2) `mintSessionCookieValue`
now carries the zone; (3) `logger.warn` on duplicate session cookies in `multi-tenant.ts`;
(4) the doc teardown below. A bricked browser **self-heals on its next sign-in** — no
delete-on-unresolvable path was needed, and adding one was deliberately rejected as risk
without coverage.

**Trap inside the fix:** the expiry must mirror the SOURCE cookie's `Secure`, not the
request's `isHttps`. Better Auth keys `useSecureCookies` on `NODE_ENV`/configured origin,
not the forwarded proto; a `Secure`-less `Set-Cookie` for a `__Secure-` name is silently
rejected, so on divergence the whole convergence no-ops. `make review-fix` (Fable) caught
this — the first cut had the bug.

**Process fix (shipped in the same PR):** `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` now tells you to clear the planted cookie
when the verification finishes, or to drive a throwaway Chrome profile. As written, every
authenticated UI verification leaves a login-bricking landmine in the human's real browser.

Diagnosis path that worked, without the claude-in-chrome extension: drive the paired Owletto
extension (`client.operations.execute`, chrome connection **479** = MacBook / worker
`709f0d3a`; 432 = Mac mini) and `evaluate` `document.cookie` + `fetch('/api/auth/get-session')`.
Note `evaluate` returns its value at `output.value`, not `output.result.value`, and
`network_intercept_*` needs `patterns` on start and `session_id` on drain/stop — and it
returns **response bodies only**, never request headers, so it cannot show you a `Cookie` header.

Related: [[reference_scrape_pin_is_not_the_human_browser]] (479 vs 432),
[[feedback_kubectl_printenv_can_silently_return_empty]].

## Summary

- A session cookie can exist at two scopes at once — host-only (`app.lobu.ai`) and domain-scoped (`Domain=.lobu.ai`). The browser sends **both**, we resolve the **first**, and RFC 6265 §5.4 orders equal-path cookies **oldest-first**. A stale host-only twin is therefore unbeatable: every later sign-in writes a strictly newer cookie that can never win, so the user is locked out with **no in-app way to recover** — re-logging-in provably cannot fix it.
- `/exchange-token` and `/local-init` were manufacturing exactly that twin in production: `mintSessionCookieValue` set the cookie **host-only** while Better Auth sets it `Domain=$AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`. `document.cookie` planting per `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` produces the same thing.
- Fix makes sign-in authoritative: whenever a response sets a domain-scoped auth cookie, it also expires the host-only twin of that name. Applied at the `/api/auth/*` chokepoint it covers Google, Slack, magic link, credential and passkey in one place — plus `state`/`pkce_code_verifier`, where a shadowed value breaks the OAuth callback rather than the session. This also **self-heals an already-bricked browser** on its next sign-in.

Measured against prod (`/api/auth/get-session`, correctly signed cookie, 2026-08-06):

| `Cookie` header | Result |
|---|---|
| `good` | session |
| `dead` | `null` |
| `dead; good` | `null` ← the brick |
| `good; dead` | session |

Also adds a `logger.warn` when one request carries the same session cookie name more than once. That state was previously **completely silent** — `get-session` just answers `200 null` forever — which is what made this cost a full debugging session.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: `make test-unit` (exit 0), targeted `bunx vitest run src/auth/__tests__/exchange-token-cookie.test.ts` (11/11)
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot behavior: ran `./scripts/test-bot.sh` or relevant eval — n/a

### red → green

New unit suite, before `src/auth/session-cookie-scope.ts` existed:

```
error: Cannot find module '../../auth/session-cookie-scope'
 0 pass
 1 fail
```

After:

```
 9 pass
 0 fail
 24 expect() calls
```

`make review-fix` (Fable; codex is quota-blocked until Aug 10) caught a real latent
no-op in the first cut and it is folded in: the expiry now mirrors the **source
cookie's** `Secure` rather than trusting this request's `isHttps`. Better Auth keys
`useSecureCookies` on `NODE_ENV`/configured origin, not on the forwarded proto, so on
divergence the browser would silently reject a `Secure`-less expiry for a `__Secure-`
name — the twin survives and the convergence does nothing. Covered by
"mirrors the source cookie's Secure even when https detection disagrees".

Wiring test, mutated (`Domain` push removed from `mintSessionCookieValue`) — proof the assertion is load-bearing and not vacuously green:

```
 × deep-link token exchange > GET /exchange-token scopes the cookie to the zone and expires the host-only twin
   → expected 'better-auth.session_token=HmSFPk4qzzi…' to contain 'Domain=.lobu.ai'
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)
```

Restored:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

## Notes

Found while diagnosing a real lockout: `emrekabakci@gmail.com` could not sign in to `app.lobu.ai` on **any** method for hours. Sessions were being minted correctly the whole time (10 rows in `session` in 24h) and the server validated them fine — the jar held a dead host-only `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` whose token had no row in `session`, and it outranked every new login.

Deliberate carve-outs, please don't "simplify" them away:
- `convergeSetCookieScope` **no-ops when no cookie zone is configured**. In local dev the host-only cookie IS the real session cookie; expiring it would log the developer out on every sign-in.
- The expiry header carries **no `Domain`** on purpose — deletion matches on (name, domain, path), so omitting it targets the twin and leaves the real cookie alone.
- The expiry keeps `Secure` even though it is a deletion: browsers reject any `Set-Cookie` for a `__Secure-`-prefixed name that lacks it, so without it the deletion silently no-ops.
- A `Set-Cookie` that is already an expiry is skipped, so sign-out is untouched.

`docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` now makes expiring the planted cookie a mandatory step — as written, every authenticated UI verification left a login-bricking cookie in the human's real browser.

Not included, deliberately: a delete-on-unresolvable path. Once sign-in converges the scope, a bricked browser heals on its next sign-in without one, and deleting cookies on an unauthenticated request is a materially riskier change for no additional coverage.
